InCad for FreeCAD - what changed
================================

This build: VERSION
Newest build first. The build name is the name of the zip file.


0.3.1
-----
Improvements
- Move Face: To also takes an edge that runs parallel to the faces (a level line, an arc, a circle)
  or a point (a corner, a work point); the faces move to its height and follow it if it moves. The
  edge or point may be on another Solid.


0.3.0
-----
Direct editing: Move Face.

New features
- New Move Face (3D Model > Modify, or right-click a face / the part): push or pull flat faces of the
  part without going back to the sketch. Pick one or more faces (they must face the same way), then
  a Distance (positive grows the part, negative cuts into it) or To a face or plane parallel to them;
  the faces move into that plane and follow it if it moves. Neighbours says what the faces next to
  the moved face do: Inventor (they keep their angle, a chamfer grows and the face gets narrower;
  holes stay holes), Step (only the face moves, a straight wall appears at a slanted neighbour's
  edge) or Together (the face and the chamfers / fillets next to it move as one piece).
- Move Face: an arrow stands on the face while the dialog is open. Drag it and the face moves with
  the preview; the Distance field follows and a label at the arrow shows the value. The arrow lights
  up under the pointer. Dragging replaces a formula or parameter in Distance with the dragged value
  in mm. With To it only shows where the face goes. Finish move on top of the right-click menu = OK.
  Distance starts at 0 mm (nothing moves until you type or drag).
- Move Face is a step in the history ("Move Face" in the browser): double-click to edit, Suppress or
  Delete like any feature; one OK is one undo step. It finds its faces again by their geometry, so
  it keeps working when an earlier feature is edited. When it cannot do the move it says why (a
  neighbour round across the move in Inventor mode, a move so large that a neighbouring face would
  vanish, a face that is no longer there, a face of another Solid) and changes nothing. Limits: flat
  faces only; in Inventor mode a neighbour that is round across the move cannot follow yet (use
  Step or Together).

Improvements
- Assembly: the gizmo arrows are a little smaller (the grab zone is as wide as before).


0.2.0
-----
Assemblies are ready to test in this build (they were untested in 0.1.x).

New features
- Assembly: drag a free part with the mouse. It moves only the way its constraints still let it
  (its own degrees of freedom); the other parts stay where they are, and a fully held part does not
  move. One drag is one undo step ("Move part").
- Assembly: click a free part to get its gizmo: an arrow for each direction it can slide, an arc for
  each axis it can turn about. Grab an arrow to slide the part, an arc to turn it. Handles are easy
  to catch (a wide grab zone on screen), the one under the pointer lights up, and the first arrow is
  up and down where the part can move that way. A click on empty space hides the gizmo.
- Assembly: each part's row in the browser shows "Grounded", "DOF n" (how many ways it can still
  move, counted against what holds it) or "DOF ?". View > Degrees of Freedom draws Inventor's DOF
  symbols on every free part; with it off, the part under the pointer shows its symbol as a tip.
- Assembly: new Parallel and Perpendicular constraints (faces or straight edges); Angle takes
  straight edges too.
- Assembly: Flip in the constraint dialogs: Mate and Flush (which way the faces face), Tangent
  (which side: outside or inside), Insert (direction), and the Rotational, Slider and Cylindrical
  joints. The preview turns the part over at once.
- Assembly: Tangent puts a round face outside the flat face's part by default.
- Assembly: the constraints in the browser (Relationships) have their own menu: Edit, Delete,
  Suppress / Unsuppress, Rename. Double-click a row to edit it. A suppressed constraint is struck
  through and its parts stay where they are. Constraint values are named after them (Mate1,
  Flush1 ...).
- Assembly: Edit on a part opens it in its own tab with the other parts of the assembly around it,
  grey and semi-transparent, at their real places (for reference only: they cannot be picked and
  are not saved). View > Assembly Context turns them off and on.
- Assembly: back in the assembly tab after editing a part, InCad asks before updating it; if you
  say no, the browser shows "Needs update" until you choose Update.
- Assembly: the browser shows each part's own history; double-click a part to open it. The part
  menu has Edit, Hide / Show, Suppress and Remove. Threads Off / On works on all parts at once.
- New Make Assembly (3D Model > Assemble, or right-click in the part): every separate piece of the
  part becomes a part file with its history, and a new assembly links them where they were (the
  largest grounded). Names are asked first; files go next to the part; the part itself stays as it
  was. Running it again offers "Replace existing files", so you don't get Train_2, Train_3 ...
- New Split (3D Model > Modify): the lines of a sketch become thin surfaces that cut the part. Keep
  all: every piece stays, each other piece as a Solid of its own (hide it, work on it, make it a
  part), still following the sketch; Keep picked: only the pieces you click stay.
- File > New Assembly in the menu. New remembers Part or Assembly; Tools > Ask on New brings the
  question back.
- Hide / Show works on Solids and assembly parts (also from their right-click menu in the browser);
  a hidden one is dimmed in the browser.
- Sketch: new Constraint List (ribbon Sketch > Constrain > List, or right-click in a sketch >
  Constraint List). It lists the sketch's constraints, including the ones with no icon to click
  (coincident points, point on a line). Pick a line or point to see only its own; select a row to
  see it in the sketch; check rows and press Delete selected (one undo step). Constraints that hold
  a sketch pattern, and dimensions used in a formula, are kept, and the window says why.
- Sketch: right-click a line or point to delete one of its constraints, or all of them.
- Sketch: projected edges are normal lines by default (as in Inventor), so they can be part of a
  profile right away. Construction switches them to construction and back. Old files follow the
  new rule in sketches nothing is built on yet.
- Hole: new Chamfer option for every hole (None / Start / Both ends, with a size): a 45° lead-in at
  the mouth of each hole and, for a through hole, at its exit. A tapped hole is chamfered from the
  thread's diameter, so a screw starts easily. With a seat (counterbore, countersink, spotface)
  only the exit can be chamfered.
- Boolean: new "Keep tool" option. Off (as it opens): the tool is used up and shows under the
  Boolean in the model tree. On: the tool stays a separate visible solid (print the pin and the box).
- Boolean: click anywhere on a solid to pick it as the base or a tool (the field names the solid,
  not the face clicked); a click on the base while picking tools is ignored. In an assembly the
  Combine button is now called Boolean too.
- Extrude: To Next goes toward the part when the default direction finds nothing; To accepts curved
  faces.
- Clearance fields say how they are measured: Boolean "Clearance (per side)", Thread and Hole
  "Print clearance (on diameter)".
- Dialogs: long choice lists wrap four buttons per row; choosing an option that needs a pick starts
  that pick, and a click on the field the dialog already made active keeps picking.

Bug fixes
- A new Solid sketched on another Solid's face took that whole Solid along with it (and Make
  Assembly then said the pieces could not be separated). It now holds only its own piece, and the
  Solid below stays shown. Older files are repaired when they are opened.
- Assembly: Mate and the other constraints picked in the 3D view sometimes lost which part a face
  belonged to, or said "can't be met" on parts placed far apart. Insert could move the grounded
  part.
- Assembly: Place asks for the part first (the save dialog for a new assembly looked like a part
  chooser).
- Delete on a Solid used by a Boolean broke the Boolean ("No source shape linked"); deleting the
  main Solid or a Split could make the other Solid vanish. Delete now asks and removes them
  together, and a pick on a piece deletes that Solid.
- A box drawn away from the part and split off into its own Solid no longer takes along what was
  built on the part after it, and sketches left on the part stay attached.
- Threads (Threads Off, Suppress) did nothing on a part with two threads when the second one was
  made after the first. Threads now attach to the hole itself; older files are repaired the first
  time threads are turned off.
- Threads Off / On left the modeled thread of a tapped Hole on (the button looked dead). It now turns
  those threads off too; the holes themselves stay.
- Threads Off / On (and Suppress on a thread) did nothing when something was made on a face of a
  later feature while the threads were off. InCad now finds the same face again by its geometry.
- Thread: choosing the Print-friendly standard sets the print clearance to 0.3 mm (0.2 mm for the
  others); a clearance you typed yourself is kept.
- Thread on a rod came out sloppy: a hair-thin fin (about 0.04 mm) stayed on every crest, worse
  when the rod was a little larger than the size (M2.5 on Ø2.594), and next to a shoulder. The rod
  is now turned down to the thread's crests first (a ThreadTrim step under the Thread); the end
  chamfers start from the part's own radius.
- Editing a thread: picks landed on the thread's own fill / bore / trim step instead of the part.
- Dialogs: a choice that becomes unavailable (after a new pick) moves to the next available one.
- Wireframe was nearly invisible in the dark theme. Its lines are now light (dark in the light
  theme) and thicker; Shaded puts the normal lines back. Switching no longer marks the file modified.
- Parameters lost their units in a file opened again (90 instead of 90°, 12 instead of 12 mm) in the
  Parameters list and in the dialogs; opening a file no longer marks its features for a recompute.


0.1.1
-----
Improvements
- Thread: any sensible size works in a hole. A Ø3 hole takes M3 (the hole is filled back to the
  M3 tap size first) or M4 (the hole is bored out to the M4 tap size first), always as a full,
  printable thread with the print clearance. The fill goes only where the hole has a wall all round,
  never into a crossing bore. A size far off the hole is still refused.
- Thread: Size "Auto" now picks the bolt that matches the hole (Ø3 -> M3, Ø4 -> M4); a tap-drill
  hole still gets its thread (Ø5.2 -> M6, Ø8.5 -> M10).
- New ribbon button "Threads" (3D Model > Modify): turns every thread off for faster work and
  redraws, and back on with a second click. A thread you turned off yourself stays off.
- Suppress / Unsuppress on a thread also turns off its chamfer and its fill or bore-out, so the
  part looks exactly as it did before the thread.

Bug fixes
- Thread on a through hole (or a rod free at both ends) started at the plain end, so the chamfered
  mouth had no thread when the thread was shorter than the hole. It now starts at the chamfered or
  rounded end.
- Thread: picking the front face as the Start face of a hole with a chamfered mouth said "The start
  face must be at one end of the threaded face". It is accepted now.
- Suppress / Unsuppress on a thread could fail with "ThreadProfile cannot be suppressed".


0.1.0
-----
First test build.
